thread.title: More than $20,000 refunded to two Wichita car buyers after fraud - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: More than $20,000 refunded to two Wichita car buyers after fraud - NewsBreak

author: Allison Campbell
title: More than $20,000 refunded to two Wichita car buyers after fraud - NewsBreak
text:
By Allison Campbell ,
3 hours ago shaunl/Getty Images Two people who bought cars from Sunset Auto Sales have been refunded about $10,000 each after a 500-plus day investigation and litigation by the Sedgwick County District Attorney’s Office.
The now-defunct used car dealership first came under investigation in 2024 after a man bought a 2006 Ford Mustang GT there as a gift for his daughter, a press release from the Sedgwick County District Attorney’s Office said. The man had paid for the car but was never given a title, which left him unable to register the Mustang.
When the car’s transmission failed he took it back to the dealership, which then failed to replace the transmission and return the car.
The purchaser filed a complaint with the District Attorney’s Office after he asked for a refund from the dealership, which made several unfulfilled promises to corrected the issues, the press release said. Another person who purchased a car from Sunset Auto Sales lodged a similar complaint soon after.
After the dealership was given “multiple opportunities to make the consumers whole” and failed to do so, Assistant District Attorney Chris Garcia filed a lawsuit against it and its manager, resulting in a settlement that caused the business to close. Both customers were repaid in full from a claim filed against the dealer’s licensing surety bond through the Kansas Department of Revenue.
The District Attorney’s Office said anyone who has been the victim of fraud or deceptive business practices should file a complaint with the DA’s Consumer Protection Division at 316-660-3600 or online at sedgwickcounty.org/district-attorney/consumer-protection-division/ .
